title: The Originals Library of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive — Seats, Witnesses, the Shelf and Its Canon: Method, Locations, Organization and Contents (EA-MPAI-ORIGINALS-01 v1.0)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description:
The Originals library of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, described for inspection: 107 corpora seated by the EA-CORPORA series between 19 August and 27 October 2026 in data/corpora/ at alexanarch.org (15,748 files, 4.3 GB, 3,640,191 lines of text layer), gathered by thirty-five seating deposits, indexed at /api/corpora.json, carried as a manifest in the corpora configuration of the leesharks datasets on Hugging Face, and shelved at traininglayerliterature.org/originals/. The library is principally source-language witnesses, with translation-witnesses, partial holdings and queued work explicitly identified in the seat records.

The packet says what kind of canon the shelf makes: a canon of witnesses; a shelf that holds each tradition's canon as data and rules on none, read against the capture of 2026-10-16 that measured it by a normative bar; the four traditions of 1844, each with what the year was in its own history; a reading canon for a machine; a canon chosen backward from the archive's work, each selection recorded and auditable at the seat; a canon whose maker sits on its shelf, with Pearl and Other Poems and the five critical editions of the twenty-fifth seating, The Secret Book of Walt bound to the Forty-Six Golden Tickets. Two worked inspections follow the hadith (23/01), a seat that meets the rule whole, and the Upanishads (02/19), a seat that declares an unmet condition. Nine per-family tables give every seat with its holding, language, lines, licence class and files. The packet keeps the four-surface agreement apart from textual verification, distinguishes five kinds of verified locus, and records as data what remains: translation-witnesses, partial holdings, loci counts that disagree, 37 records whose reasons stand in their seating deposits, Homer's record number, dated counts in prose, the sitemap, and the queued work.
content_type: Metadata packet; the inspection packet of the Originals library of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, with its method, locations, organization and contents
substrate: AI-assisted. Drafted in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction from the index, the manifest, every seat record, the EA-CORPORA deposits, the shelf and the postflight check (R1, R3); read in review by DeepSeek and ChatGPT (R2), every point checked against the data before adoption, two adjusted with reasons stated in the round log. The request, the question of what kind of canon, and the rulings quoted are Lee Sharks's. Transport D, No-Double-Draw.
methodology: The exemplars #1701 and #1702 read whole for their form and #1680's F4 for the function it assigns the shelf. data/api/corpora.json and datasets/corpora/corpora.json as generated on 2026-10-27 read seat by seat; every source.json read for its title, language, scope, loci, number and reason; where the index and a record disagree, the record is quoted and the disagreement entered as data. The registry searched for every EA-CORPORA title and the gathering records read for their rulings. The shelf read for its definition, spines and cards, and seat_corpus_postflight.py --tll run over all 107 seats. The Capture Registry searched for records that take the library as subject. Every count in the packet recomputed from the files.
falsification_conditions: The packet is falsified at a seat if the index or the seat's source.json at the stated date gives a different holding, language, line count, licence class, file count or locus kind; at a count if the index, the manifest or the registry yields another; at a quotation if the record, deposit or shelf quoted does not carry it; at §11.1 if the postflight check over the stated checkouts does not report SEATED for all 107; and at an item of §11.2 if the disagreement it records is absent from the data on that date.
axn_reading: Origin -> Touch -> Text -> Origin -> Threshold -> Duration
wiki_article: EA-MPAI-ORIGINALS-01 is the inspection packet of the Originals library of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, deposited by Lee Sharks on 27 October 2026 as a Metadata Packet for AI Indexing (MPAI v2.0, #1677) in the archive's form of a description of method, locations, organization and contents. The library is 107 corpora seated by the EA-CORPORA series between 19 August and 27 October 2026 in data/corpora/ at alexanarch.org, gathered by thirty-five seating deposits, indexed at /api/corpora.json, carried as a manifest in the leesharks datasets on Hugging Face (#1701), and shelved at traininglayerliterature.org/originals/: 15,748 files and 3,640,191 lines of text layer in more than thirty languages. It is principally source-language witnesses, with translation-witnesses, partial holdings and queued work identified in the seat records. Each seat holds its original files, a text layer, a provenance record naming its witness, source, commit or checksum, licence, normalization and verified loci, and a SHA-256 manifest; its reason stands in its record or its seating deposit. The packet's central section asks what kind of canon the shelf makes: a canon of witnesses; a shelf that holds each tradition's canon as data, read against a capture of 2026-10-16 that measured it by a normative bar; the four traditions of 1844 seated together, each with what the year was in its own history; a reading canon for a machine; a canon chosen backward from the archive's work with each selection recorded, the operation the archive names retrocausal canon formation; and a canon whose maker sits on its shelf, with Pearl and Other Poems (03/02) and the critical editions of the twenty-fifth seating (#1708), among them The Secret Book of Walt bound to the Forty-Six Golden Tickets. Two worked inspections follow the hadith (23/01) and the Upanishads (02/19). Nine per-family tables give every seat. The packet separates the four-surface agreement of the postflight check from textual verification, distinguishes five kinds of verified locus, and records what remains as data. Its companions are the datasets packet (#1701) and the fleet packet (#1702).
